findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: After a successful deleteCache mutation, the component never invalidates the trpc query that populated `cacheUpdatedAt`. Compare with the disconnectMutation further down which calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled`. Without an invalidation, after the user confirms cache deletion the UI continues to show the same 'Last updated' timestamp (the deleted row's data is still in the React Query cache) until some other action triggers a refetch. The proper fix is to also invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` from deleteCache's `onSettled` (or `onSuccess`) so the timestamp updates immediately.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data is a no-op
findings.body: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` passes an empty `data` object. Prisma's `@updatedAt` directive only fires when actual fields change, so calling `updateMany` with `{}` does nothing — no row is touched and `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is NOT bumped, contrary to the comment immediately above it. The call either needs an explicit field set (e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`) or should be removed if there is no `@updatedAt` column on `SelectedCalendar`. As written it silently does nothing on every cache refresh.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt
findings.body: `getCachedAvailability` (line ~95) filters cache rows by `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` so only fresh entries are treated as cache hits. The new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` does not — it just groups all rows. The UI surfaces the result as 'Cache Status / Last updated', which now reports a timestamp even for cache entries that have already expired and would never be served. This is inconsistent with the read path and will mislead users into thinking they have a fresh cache when there is none. Add an `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` filter (or document explicitly that the status is intentionally historical).

findings.title: Existing rows get DEFAULT NOW() which misrepresents staleness
findings.body: The migration sets `updatedAt TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`. For every existing CalendarCache row that has not been rewritten by Prisma since the migration, the column is set to the moment the migration ran, not to the actual last cache write time. Combined with `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, this surfaces a misleading 'Last updated: <few minutes ago>' for legacy cache that could be weeks old. Consider backfilling `updatedAt` from a closer proxy (`expiresAt - INTERVAL '30 days'` or the existing last write timestamp if available) so the UI's 'Last updated' is meaningful for legacy data.

findings.title: sed syntax is macOS/BSD-only
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses BSD sed's `sed -i ''` (empty-string backup suffix) convention, which is a no-op (or 'unknown command') on GNU sed. On Linux the script will silently fail to update `.env`, then `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` will still point at the old tunnel/port and Google webhooks will misroute. Either use `sed -i.bak ...; rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"` or write the file with a portable tool (printf/awk) or branch on `uname -s`.

findings.title: Non-interactive cache status is wrapped in DropdownMenuItem
findings.body: Lines 84-97 wrap a purely informational 'Cache Status / Last updated …' block in a `<DropdownMenuItem>`. `DropdownMenuItem` is the clickable element of a radix dropdown menu — clicking it (which users naturally do to try to focus/read it) triggers the dropdown's selection handler and closes the menu, hiding the very information they were looking at. Wrap the static text in a plain `<div>` (or a `<DropdownMenuLabel>`) so the dropdown stays open. The second `<DropdownMenuItem>` further down is the real action and is fine.
